headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGen’s writable, executable workspace can conflict with Superset’s API-driven data workflows, while prompt-injection and compliance risks remain limited by missing shared channels and data-class overlap.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGen can read/write files and use stdin/stdout, while Superset exposes a Superset API and allowlisted egress. No shared channel is documented, so direct injection is not provable; the plausible bridge is manual file or text handoff, which is lower blast radius than default shared-memory paths.
conditions: IF the operator copies AutoGen-generated text into Superset inputs or dashboards
IF both agents are configured to share a filesystem or message queue
mitigations: Keep agents in separate workspaces
Disable copy-paste handoff for untrusted content
Add a human review step before any Superset ingestion
Use read-only exports between agents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to all inter-agent artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGen touches application data and model-provider API keys, and can write/read configured working directories. Superset’s profile shows no data classes touched and only allowlisted egress. With no shared workspace or sensitive data class on B, leakage is plausible only through operator-shared files, so blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the same working directory contains secrets or application data for both agents
IF the operator routes sensitive files from AutoGen into Superset uploads or queries
mitigations: Separate secrets from shared workspaces
Mount Superset on a different directory tree
Rotate any exposed API keys
Review file permissions on the AutoGen workspace
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGen has execute_shell, install_packages, spawn_subprocesses, and write_filesystem; Superset has allowlisted network egress and API access. Even without explicit Superset write permissions, overlapping mutable surfaces can still collide through shared files or API-driven state, and the profiles do not show locking or coordination.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF Superset API actions mutate shared datasets while AutoGen edits files in the same workflow
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize writes with a simple operator lock
Avoid concurrent runs during state changes
Snapshot files before AutoGen edits them
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGen can generate code, plans, or facts from tool use, and Superset can consume API-driven inputs or render downstream analytics. The profiles do not show verification gates between them, so if Superset treats AutoGen output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect dashboards or actions.
conditions: IF Superset ingests AutoGen output without validation
IF AutoGen-produced summaries are used as source data for dashboards or alerts
mitigations: Require manual validation before ingestion
Compare outputs against source records
Label AutoGen output as untrusted
Use checksum or schema checks on transferred data
requires-engineering: add verification middleware between agents

E_compliance.rationale: AutoGen explicitly handles model-provider API keys and application data, while Superset’s profile does not declare regulated data classes or residency constraints. Because no PHI/EU PII or retention mismatch is documented, compliance risk is limited to operator misconfiguration rather than a default breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workflow
IF the operator configures Superset or AutoGen to retain data beyond policy
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in the pair
Document retention settings for both tools
Review access logs after each run
Purge temporary files promptly
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
